results.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
results.proof_sketch: An induced cycle of length at least 10 contains an induced P8 on eight consecutive vertices. Bipartiteness excludes odd cycles, so the only induced cycles are C4, C6, and C8. Every cyclic graph contains a chordless cycle, obtained by choosing a shortest cycle. Hence hitting these three kinds of induced cycles is equivalent to being a feedback vertex set. Every path in a tree is induced, so a tree induced in a P8-free graph has diameter at most 6 and therefore radius at most 3. Finally, if x belongs to an inclusion-minimal feedback vertex set, restoring x must create a cycle. Since G-S is a forest, that cycle consists of x and the unique path between two neighbors of x lying in the same tree component.

results.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
results.proof_sketch: Enumerate all vertex subsets of sizes 4, 6, and 8 and retain those inducing cycles. By the first claim, this rank-eight hypergraph has exactly the feedback vertex sets as its transversals. For the exact algorithm, choose any remaining hyperedge C. Every size-k solution contains some vertex of C, so branch into at most eight instances, selecting one vertex of C and decreasing k. The recursion has at most 8^k leaves. For approximation, greedily construct a maximal family of vertex-disjoint induced cycles and return their union U. Maximality makes U a feedback vertex set. If the family has p cycles, every feedback vertex set has size at least p, while |U|≤8p.

results.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
results.proof_sketch: The finite structural lemma used here was checked exhaustively: a C4-free P8-free bipartite graph cannot contain a simple path on 15 vertices. For a fixed ordered Hamilton path v1,…,vq, the checker introduces vertices in order. Bipartiteness determines the allowable earlier neighbors and forces the path predecessor. An extension is rejected exactly when two selected neighbors already have a common neighbor, creating a C4, or when an eight-set containing the new vertex induces P8. Earlier violations cannot be repaired by later vertices. The numbers of surviving ordered graphs for q=1,…,14 are 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3, and none extends to q=15. Thus any hypothetical 15-vertex path would induce one of the exhaustively rejected Hamilton-path graphs. Now run undirected DFS. Every graph edge joins an ancestor-descendant pair, and every root-to-leaf path has at most 14 vertices. Taking, for each DFS vertex, the bag consisting of it and all its ancestors gives a tree decomposition of width at most 13. A constant-width dynamic program recording deleted bag vertices and the connectivity partition of retained vertices computes an exact minimum FVS.

results.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
results.proof_sketch: Find a C4-transversal X of size at most r by repeatedly choosing a C4 and branching on its four vertices. This costs O(4^r n^{O(1)}). The induced graph G-X is still bipartite and P8-free and is now C4-free, so the preceding claim supplies a width-13 decomposition. Add all of X to every bag, obtaining a decomposition of G of width at most r+13. On a nice version of this decomposition, a standard explicit forest dynamic program stores which bag vertices are deleted and a partition describing connectivity among retained vertices. An introduced edge is rejected if it closes a component, and join states are accepted only when their union stays acyclic. There are 2^{O(r log r)} states per bag.

results.claim: Several natural routes from these reductions to the full result are blocked by explicit P8-free families: C4-transversal number is unbounded even after removing false twins; 2-connected C4-free blocks have unbounded order; and the short-cycle LP is not integral.
results.proof_sketch: Let H_n have parts {a1,…,an},{b1,…,bn} and edge a_i b_j exactly when i≤j. Its neighborhoods are strictly nested, so it is false-twin-free and 2K2-free, hence P5-free. Its minimum FVS and C4-transversal number are n-2: retaining all b_j together with a_{n-1},a_n gives a forest of size n+2. Conversely, if a_i,a_j are the two retained A-vertices of smallest indices, i<j, C4-freeness permits at most one retained b_l with l≥j. Thus at most j vertices of B and n-j+2 of A remain. Next, Θ_m formed from m internally disjoint paths u-a_i-b_i-v is bipartite, false-twin-free, 2-connected, and has unbounded order. Every induced path has at most six vertices, while deleting u makes it a tree. Finally, K_{n,n} is P4-free and has optimum FVS n-1. In the LP with one constraint per induced cycle, assigning 1/4 to every vertex is optimal with value n/2, giving integrality gap 2-2/n.

final_writeup:
The full polynomial-time algorithm is not established. The main rigorous progress is an exact reduction to a polynomial-size rank-eight transversal instance, an O(8^k n^8) parameterized algorithm, and an exact polynomial algorithm for the entire C4-free subclass. The latter rests on a reproducible finite lemma giving the explicit bound treewidth≤13, rather than merely an unspecified bounded-width conclusion. Adding a C4-transversal to every decomposition bag extends this to an exact FPT algorithm parameterized by that transversal number.

The unresolved portion is the regime containing many overlapping C4s. This cannot be dismissed through bounded twin quotient or bounded C4-transversal: the twin-free half graphs H_n are already P5-free and have C4-transversal number n-2. Nor can one enumerate bounded-size 2-connected blocks, as the family Θ_m shows. Finally, even on complete bipartite graphs the direct cycle-cover LP has a gap approaching two. Thus the short-cycle formulation is exact and useful, but an additional decomposition or optimization principle for the dense C4 regime is still required.
